title: Chapter 14 Quiz
description: Final review: HTML semantics, CSS fundamentals, layout, responsive design, and accessibility!

questions.question: Which element is NOT a semantic landmark?
questions.explanation: <div> is a generic container; it has no inherent semantic meaning.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `alt` attribute on an ``?
options: To describe the image for screen readers and when the image fails to load
To set an alternative image source
questions.explanation: `alt` provides text alternative for accessibility and fallback.

questions.question: The CSS property that makes width/height include padding and border is ______.
questions.explanation: `box-sizing: border-box;` includes padding and border in the element's dimensions.

questions.question: Which selector has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: #id has specificity 0,1,0,0, higher than class or type.

questions.question: How do you centre a block element horizontally with CSS?
questions.explanation: `margin: 0 auto;` works on block elements with a defined width.

questions.question: Which Flexbox property distributes space along the main axis?
questions.explanation: `justify-content` aligns items along the main axis.

questions.question: What does `grid-template-areas` allow you to do?
options: Create a visual layout by naming grid cells
questions.explanation: `grid-template-areas` lets you design the layout using named area strings.

questions.question: Flexbox is designed for two-dimensional layouts (rows and columns simultaneously).
questions.explanation: Flexbox is one-dimensional; Grid handles two dimensions.

questions.question: Which media query targets screens 768px and wider?
questions.explanation: `min-width: 768px` applies when viewport is 768px or more.

questions.question: What is the best way to provide different image resolutions for different screen densities?
questions.explanation: `srcset` and `sizes` let the browser choose the best image.

questions.question: Using CSS animations, you should respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
questions.explanation: Disabling or reducing animations for users who prefer reduced motion is an accessibility requirement.

questions.question: Which HTML element is used to group form controls and provide a caption?
questions.explanation: <fieldset> groups controls, and <legend> provides the caption.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using `rem` units over `px` for font sizes?
options: They scale with the user's browser font size setting
questions.explanation: `rem` respects user preferences, enhancing accessibility.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a valid pseudo‑class?
questions.explanation: `:first-letter` is a pseudo‑element (uses `::`).

questions.question: The universal box‑sizing reset should include `*` and also `*::before` and `*::______`.
questions.explanation: Include both pseudo‑elements to ensure consistent sizing.

questions.question: What is a skip‑to‑content link?
options: A hidden link that becomes visible on focus, allowing keyboard users to bypass navigation
questions.explanation: It's an accessibility feature for keyboard users to jump to main content.

questions.question: In mobile‑first responsive design, where do you put the base styles?
options: Outside any media queries (smallest screen styles)
questions.explanation: Base styles are for the smallest screens; media queries add complexity for larger screens.

questions.question: CSS transitions require a trigger like `:hover`; animations can play automatically.
questions.explanation: Transitions react to state changes; animations run independently.

questions.question: Which property would you use to create a fade‑in effect when an element appears?
questions.explanation: `opacity` transition from 0 to 1 creates a fade.

questions.question: What is a key benefit of using CSS custom properties (variables)?
options: They allow values to be reused and updated globally
questions.explanation: Custom properties define reusable design tokens.

questions.question: When debugging a layout, what tool helps visualise the box model?
options: Elements panel → Computed / Box Model diagram
questions.explanation: DevTools shows the box model visually, including content, padding, border, margin.

questions.question: What does `container-type: inline-size;` enable?
options: Container queries that style elements based on parent width
questions.explanation: Container queries let you respond to a container's size, not just viewport.

questions.question: It's acceptable to use `!important` regularly to manage specificity.
questions.explanation: Overuse of `!important` leads to unmaintainable code; it should be a last resort.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid HTML5 form validation attribute?
questions.explanation: `required` makes a field mandatory before submission.
